title: Concerning the Three Creations of the Flesh: the ones that were brought forth [...]; and the ones that were begotten by the Abortions; and the ones that were formed of themselves.
teaching_text:
Once again our enlightener speaks to his disciples:

“All these animals that you see, and also the rest of the [crea]tures [...] of the earth, confirm them in three likeness[es ...]: some from [...] abortions. Others, however, form their own selves in their shape [...].

“Also, their nourishment is thre[e ...] light in them, if they shall wish [...]. [...] they eat see[ds and] fr[uit ...]; they eat seeds and fruit. The [...] it entirely, and they [...] the three archetyp[es] from their nature and the [...] the time when they are on the ea[rth ...]; they are seized [...] in their [...]. The Ambassador [...] all powers [...].

“[N] it [...], first [...]. ⟨p.247⟩ Plant them generally to this name: shoots and grass. It formed the bad, bitter trees, the reeds and the thorns and the [...] and these others that are like them.

“For that thought belongs to the flesh-eating rulers. Still, these [that were] planted (belong to) grass and gourds, since they are in their essence. Nevertheless, [this t]ho[ugh]t that came down from the rulers, as they are in fruit and grass first and shall not be planted in flesh and blood, it formed the trees that shall give nourishing fru[it], as their gourds are sweet.

“Again, this thou[ght] that came down from the powers that eat m[ea]t and also eat grass and gourds, it has formed the trees that shall not produce any nourishment. Their fruits belong neither to good nor evil.”
gardner_synopsis: This chapter shows again how Mani presented his teaching as an integrated science for understanding the entire world. Life arises from the mixed light and dross that fell to earth at the time when the Ambassador displayed his image in the heavens, and the demonic powers ejaculated or aborted in their lust. This matter or sin contained the 'thought' (¿veuunotc) or driving force that causes reproduction. Here Mani attempts to classify the different forms of plant life according to various means of propagation.
editorial_notes: Source contained an intrusion from the following chapter (“CHAPTER NINETY-EIGHT …”) after a stray page number “253”; this entire block has been excluded from Chapter 97. Manuscript line-number ticks (5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, etc.) were removed where they interrupted the English. Coptic line-break markers “/” were removed and broken words rejoined (e.g., ‘crea]/tur[es’ → ‘[crea]tures’; ‘th[oug]/ht’ → ‘thought’). Running headers/page artifacts were removed; the in-text manuscript page marker “(247)” was converted to ⟨p.247⟩. Lacunae markers [...] and editorial restorations in square brackets were preserved as given. Some clauses remain syntactically difficult because the exemplar has multiple lacunae; no conjectural wording was added.
